'''Shai Haran''' ({{Langx|he|שי הרן}}; born 1958) is an Israeli mathematician and professor at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shai Haran - Faculty of Mathematics |url=https://math.technion.ac.il/en/tg_members/shai-haran/ |access-date=November 19, 2023 |website=Technion - Faculty of Mathematics}}</ref> He is known for his work in [[p-adic analysis]], [[p-adic quantum mechanics]], and [[non-additive geometry]], including the [[field with one element]], in relation to strategies for proving the [[Riemann Hypothesis]].

== Life ==

Born in Jerusalem on October 8, 1958, Haran graduated from the [[Hebrew University]] in 1979, and, in 1983, received his PhD in mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) on "p-Adic L-functions for Elliptic Curves over CM Fields"<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shai Haran - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=64471 |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> under his advisor [[Barry Mazur]] from [[Harvard University]], and his mentors [[Michael Artin]] and [[Daniel Quillen]] from MIT.

Haran is a professor at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]]. He was a frequent visitor at [[Stanford University]], MIT, Harvard and [[Columbia University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=ScheduleJointNTS35.html |url=http://www.math.columbia.edu/~goldfeld/ScheduleJointNTS39.html |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=www.math.columbia.edu}}</ref> the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]], [[Max-Planck Institute]], [[Kyushu University]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=STUDENTS & GUESTS |url=https://imi.kyushu-u.ac.jp/~wakayama/estudent_guest.html |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=imi.kyushu-u.ac.jp}}</ref> and the [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]], among other institutions.

== Work ==

His early work was in the construction of [[p-adic L-function]]s for [[modular form]]s on GL(2) over any number field.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haran |first=Shai |date=1987 |title=p-adic L-functions for modular forms. |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=CM_1987__62_1_31_0 |journal=Compositio Mathematica |volume=62 |issue=1 |pages=31–46}}</ref> He gave a formula for the explicit sums of arithmetic functions expressing in a uniform way the contribution of a prime, finite or real, as the derivative at <math>\alpha=0</math>  of the [[Riesz potential]] of order <math>\alpha</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haran |first=Shai |date=1990 |title=Riesz potentials and explicit sums in arithmetic |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01231521 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume=101 |pages=697–703|doi=10.1007/BF01231521 |bibcode=1990InMat.101..697H |s2cid=120622541 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This formula is one of the inspirations<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last=Benjamin |first=Clare |date=14 Aug 2008 |title=[0808.1965] Nonstandard Mathematics and New Zeta and L-Functions |page=141 "This is very similar to the work of Connes, in fact he has rewritten the global trace formulas using the tools of non-commutative geometry."|class=math.NT |eprint=0808.1965 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Van Frankenhuysen |first=Machiel |title=The Riemann hypothesis for function fields: Frobenius flow and shift operators |date=2014 |publisher=Cambridge university press |isbn=978-1-107-04721-1 |series=London Mathematical Society student texts |location=Cambridge |pages=4 "Recently, Alain Connes found a completely new method again, based on the work of Shai Haran"}}</ref> for the non-commutative geometry approach to the Riemann Hypothesis of [[Alain Connes]]. He then developed potential theory<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haran |first=Shai |date=1993 |title=Analytic potential theory over the p-adics. |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=AIF_1993__43_4_905_0 |journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=905–944|doi=10.5802/aif.1361 }}</ref> and quantum mechanics over the p-adic numbers,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haran |first=Shai |date=1993 |title=Quantizations and symbolic calculus over the p-adic numbers |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=AIF_1993__43_4_997_0 |journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=997–1053|doi=10.5802/aif.1363 }}</ref> and is currently an editor of the journal "''p-Adic Numbers, Ultrametric Analysis and Applications"'' <ref>{{Cite web |title=p-Adic Numbers, Ultrametric Analysis and Applications |url=https://www.springer.com/journal/12607/editors |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=Springer |language=en}}</ref>''.''

Haran also studied the tree structure of the [[P-adic number|p-adic integers]] within the real and complex numbers and showed that it is given by the theory of classic [[orthogonal polynomials]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Haran |first=Shai |title=The mysteries of the real prime. |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2001 |isbn=0-19-850868-9 |location=New York}}</ref> He constructed [[Markov chain]]s over the p-adic, real, and complex numbers, giving finite approximations to the harmonic beta measure. In particular, he showed that there is a [[q-analog]]ue theory that interpolates between the p-adic theory and the real and complex theory. With his students Uri Onn and Uri Badder, he developed the higher rank theory for GL(n).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Haran |first=Shai |title=Arithmetical investigations. Representation theory, orthogonal polynomials, and quantum interpolations |publisher=Lecture Notes in Math.1941, Springer-Verlag, Berlin |year=2008 |isbn=978-3-540-78378-7}}</ref>

His recent work is focused on the development of mathematical foundations for non-additive geometry, a geometric theory that is not based on commutative rings.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haran |first=Shai |date=2007 |title=Non-additive geometry |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/compositio-mathematica/article/nonadditive-geometry/6CAE381F00E5ABD34DB232D69B71ADCF |journal=  Compositio Mathematica|volume=143 |issue=3 |pages=618–688|doi=10.1112/S0010437X06002624 }}</ref> In this theory, the field with one element <math>\mathbb{F}</math> is defined as the category of finite sets with partial bijections, or equivalently, of finite [[pointed set]]s with maps that preserve the distinguished points. The non-additive geometry is then developed using two languages,  <math>\mathbb{F}-\mathcal{R}\text{ings}</math> and "generalized rings", to replace  commutative rings in usual algebraic geometry. In this theory, it is possible to consider the [[Compactification (mathematics)|compactification]] of the spectrum of <math>\mathbb{Z}</math> and a model for the arithmetic plane that does not reduce to the diagonal <math>\mathbb{Z}</math>.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Absolute arithmetic and F1-geometry |date=2016 |publisher=European Mathematical Society |isbn=978-3-03719-157-6 |editor-last=Thas |editor-first=Koen |location=Zürich |pages=166. "Similarly, Haran definition of a generalized scheme (...)"}}</ref>
